across [roadway] s/b and failed to yield right of way - motor vehicle, causing unit 1 to collide front concentrated (front right area) to unit 2/pedestrian right side of body. unit 2/pedestrian head and upper body struck unit 1 front windshield, causing damage to the windshield. unit 2/[roadway] and struck her head on the southwest curb of the roadway, then traveled southeast, along the curb to her rest location. unit 1 left the location without stopping to render aid to unit 2/pedestrian. dallas fire rescue 06 arrived on scene and found unit 2/pedestrian to have no signs of life at 2:47am on [date]. unit 1 driver was returned to the scene by her boyfriend approximately two hours after the crash. i/o was able to interview unit 1 driver at the scene, then i/o was able to inspect the damages to unit 1 at another location. i/o interviewed three witnesses at the scene and they said that they were [roadway] and saw unit 2/pedestrian in the [roadway], so they stopped to tell to her [roadway], but that unit 2/pedestrian started to yell profanities at them. they said that they drove away, then returned to tell unit 2/pedestrian [roadway] a second time, but that unit 2/pedestrian started to hit the driver window, so they drove away again. they said that they returned to the location to call 911 and to keep an eye on unit 2/pedestrian from the nearby cross-street, then they saw unit 1 hit unit 2/pedestrian and unit 1 kept going. the information for the three witnesses is documented in the related offense report, [case id]. traffic sgt price 7464, vcu det smith 5956, vcu det jackson 5786 responded to the scene. crime scene element [identifier] responded to the scene and took photographs. field investigator v. resendiz from the dallas county medical examiners office detected. i/o added a contributing factor of 67 - under the influence of alcohol and a contributing factor of 68 - under the influence of drug to this report for unit 2/pedestrian. this report is now complete. **********

pedestrian (unit#2) was coming from the north side of the roadway crossing the westbound lanes of [roadway]. driver#1 stated he already began to slow down because the [roadway]. driver#1 stated it appeared the pedestrian was going to cross into his lanes so he slowed down even more. driver#1 stated as he got closer to the pedestrian, the pedestrian threw a beer can at the windshield of his fully marked unit. driver#1 stated the pedestrian crossed the front of unit#1 but then backed up into unit#1 as if he was attempting to get struck and was hit by the passenger side mirror of unit#1. driver#1 called the incident in to plano pd communications, moments later notified everyone that the pedestrian was now running and ran into the tom thumb grocery store. the pedestrian was not very cooperative. the pedestrian had an odor of an alcoholic beverage. the cover of the passenger mirror was broken off and there was damage to the right side of unit#1 just above the right front tire. i contacted the manager of the texaco gas station because it appeared the pedestrian may have come from that location purchasing beer. the manager, aashish aman (469. 443. 0212) stated he was in his car sleeping waiting for the time to open the gas station when he was abruptly woken up by the pedestrian banging on his car window with the beer can. aman stated it was a budweiser beer can that was not opened. aman stated he yelled at the pedestrian to get out here or he will called the police. aman stated he went in the store to open and saw the pedestrian walking around in the parking lot for a few minutes. aman stated the next time he saw the pedestrian, he (pedestrian) was in front of the pollo regio with the pisd police officer. aman did not see when the pedestrian entered the roadway and was not aware of the crash. as of now there has been no video evidence of the crash. the pedestrian was arrested for public intoxication and an outstanding misdemeanor warrant from dallas pd. the beer can was never located. update 5/12/2022this crash has been in the system showing to be waiting on lab results. there was no lab test done because there was no blood drawn for public intoxication. this case is closed.

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] at approximately 2100 hours officer adams [roadway] garland dallas county, texas (@ quick trip) in reference to an accident. upon arrival officer was met by matthew moody w/m [date]. moody was grabbing his leg and stated that he had been struck by a vehicle. moody was talking loudly and was very excitable. officer adams observed moody to have the strong smell of an alcoholic beverage on his breath and person. moody's eyes were red and glassy. moody explained to officer adams that he was walking through the parking lot when he was struck by a vehicle. moody began stating over and over that he didn't know what to do. officer asked moody if he wished for medical first responders (garland fire department) to respond to the scene and he said no. officer adams then explained that he could complete an accident report for moody. officer attempted to gather moody's information, but he just keep asking what am i supposed to do and how do we handle this. officer again attempted to explain to moody that he was completing an accident report for him, but moody seemed to not comprehend. in the middle of gathering moody's information he quit listening to officer all together and made a phone call. officer adams then spoke with the driver of the vehicle (2002 toyota 4-runner, silver in color, texas kcs-4081) that struck moody, brian villa h/m [date]. brian advised he was backing/reversing to leave the location, when he heard a small noise from the rear of the vehicle. brian investigated and observed moody. moody stated he had been struck by brian's vehicle. brian advised a small verbal altercation occurred, but it was quickly squashed. officer adams then spoke with quick trip management, who allowed him to view the surveillance video of the crash. the video shows moody walking toward the store. moody gets into some type of verbal altercation with a passing vehicle, and throws his hands up at the vehicle as they are driving away. moody then stumbles backwards and makes contact with brian's vehicle, which is backing/reversing. the collision seemed to be very minor. moody can be seen walking around the passenger side of brian's vehicle. moody showed no initial visible signs of being injured on the video. through routine check and confirmation, moody was found to have active warrants for his arrest (rowlett pd warrant info 180006248 - open container/alcohol - passenger - 372. 00 bond). moody was placed into custody in one set of double-locked handcuffs, which were checked for fit. moody was then transported to the garland jail, where he was booked without incident.

uninvolved by-stander who had simply stopped to assist ped after the collision . ped was assessed by ems who had determined that any alleged or perceived injury did not require immediate transport
